blocker.summary: r461 fixed the 'render target region exceeds the bounded size' rejection named by r460's second track. A live trace showed scissor_tl=0x0 scissor_br=0x20002000, a (0,0)-(8192,8192) region -- the standard Xenos/GPU scissor-test idiom for 'no extra clipping' (real hardware clamps rasterization to the actual render target regardless of a nominally larger scissor rect), unlike r459's EDRAM-tile-under-MSAA question which had no citable evidence. Fixed by reordering the tile-pitch geometry computation (pitch_tiles/image_width/image_height/origin_x/origin_y, which never depended on the scissor) before the scissor region calculation, then clamping the scissor to the real surface bounds (image_width - origin_x / image_height - origin_y) instead of rejecting against the arbitrary kMaxEdramRegionWidth/Height constant -- reusing the exact same geometry the existing final bounds check already depends on, not a new formula. Verified: native ctest 11/11, no regression, and a live probe confirms the targeted rejection is gone (0 occurrences); presented_frames and capture are unchanged. The previously-rejected draw now progresses further and reaches a 'clip_disable viewport path not qualified this cycle' gate that was never reachable before (the scissor rejection always short-circuited first) -- not yet investigated. Named for r462: (1) the pinned registry coverage gap (r456) likely needs an oracle session -- user decision, not to be spent unilaterally; (2) the newly-reachable clip_disable gate, not yet investigated -- could be another targeted fix (same pattern as r457/r460/r461) or a real coverage gap. Still open, non-blocking: once the wiring is judged mature, reconsider the backlog commit decision (r433/r434/r438/r454-r461); update tools/prepare.py/build.py to default to the current ISO path (r452/r453, convenience only).
